screens.audience: Developers evaluating Spec4 / learners arriving at the gallery
screens.purpose: Explain what BWS4 is, state its Spec4 provenance, and present the roster of example apps ordered simplest-first.
Show retrieval-augmented generation with retrieved passages visible alongside the grounded answer.

screens.audience: Developers learning tool use / function calling
screens.purpose: Show an agent deciding to call a shared web search tool mid-response and synthesising from the returned snippets.

screens.audience: Developers learning the baseline single-call pattern
screens.purpose: Show one prompt in / one response out in both plain and schema-conforming modes.
Show two sequential model calls where the second consumes the first's output, with both stages visible.

screens.audience: Developers learning the plan-first planning-agent pattern
screens.purpose: Show a planner call decomposing a goal into a reviewable plan, then executor calls running it after explicit go-ahead; contrast plan-first with the interleaved ReAct loop.

screens.audience: Developers learning the interleaved reason-act-observe pattern
screens.purpose: Show a live ReAct trace where each next step follows the previous observation, contrasted explicitly with the plan-first Planning Agent example, ending in either a final answer or an honest budget-exhausted card.
Show a coordinator choosing exactly two of four specialists, briefing each, running them concurrently, and merging their answers.
Show one buyer agent negotiating a single procurement round against two rival sellers with code-enforced message opacity, ending in an award and a reveal.
Show curated texts clustering by meaning in a fixed 2D projection and let visitors place their own text on the same plot.
Exercise the shared framework capabilities directly, watch usage allowances move, and inspect the cross-app request log.

surfaces.output: Short educational overview of the retrieval-augmented generation pattern.

surfaces.output: Submits the question and hands off to the answer surface.

surfaces.output: Short educational overview of tool use / function calling.

surfaces.output: Submitted query passed to the search tool trace.

surfaces.name: singlecall_overview
surfaces.output: Short educational overview of the single-call pattern and when it suits a problem.

surfaces.name: singlecall_prompt_form
surfaces.output: One submitted prompt plus chosen response mode.

surfaces.name: singlecall_result
surfaces.output: Plain-text response, or in structured mode the request with its schema alongside the returned object and a conformance verdict.

surfaces.name: chained_overview
surfaces.output: Educational overview of chained calls plus the plainly-stated two-call quota rationale.

surfaces.output: Submitted story prompt plus a two-step role rail showing each stage's declared role.

surfaces.name: chained_stage_results
surfaces.output: Intermediate writer draft and final critic critique, both labelled with their stage role.
surfaces.affordance: show multi-step progress/status while it runs

surfaces.name: planning_overview
inputs: cross-reference link to the ReAct Loop example
surfaces.output: Educational overview of the plan-first planning-agent pattern, the quota rationale, and an explicit contrast with the interleaved reason-act-observe ReAct Loop example with a link to it.

surfaces.name: planning_goal_form
surfaces.output: Submitted goal (city + interests) plus visible remaining-runs count.

surfaces.name: planning_plan_review
surfaces.output: The proposed plan of discrete steps with kind and purpose, awaiting explicit go-ahead; trimmed-plan warning when the planner over-produced.
surfaces.affordance: require explicit confirmation before the action commits

invocation.trigger: Two-phase: (1) user submits city + interests in the example app UI, which invokes the planner call and returns the displayed plan; (2) user's explicit advance signal triggers sequential execution of the planned steps.

surfaces.name: planning_execution_trace
surfaces.output: Per-step status and result appearing one by one, ending in the one-day itinerary with morning / afternoon / evening sections and any honest research gap noted.
surfaces.affordance: show multi-step progress/status while it runs; surface results as each step completes

invocation.trigger: Two-phase: (1) user submits city + interests in the example app UI, which invokes the planner call and returns the displayed plan; (2) user's explicit advance signal triggers sequential execution of the planned steps.

surfaces.name: react_overview
inputs: cross-reference link to the Planning Agent example
surfaces.output: Educational overview of the interleaved reason-act-observe loop, its explicit contrast with the plan-first Planning Agent example (with a link) and with a single decision about whether to search, the note that on familiar presets the model may state an early hop from memory, and the two-runs-per-visit quota rationale.

surfaces.name: react_question_form
surfaces.output: Selected preset or typed question plus the cycle budget for the run, with remaining runs shown.
states: runs exhausted (inputs and start disabled, prior results retained)
surfaces.affordance: show multi-step progress/status while it runs

invocation.trigger: Visitor opens the ReAct Loop example, selects one of five curated multi-hop presets or types their own question, sets a cycle budget, and presses Start; frontend calls POST /api/react/run

surfaces.name: react_suitability_check
surfaces.output: An advisory verdict on a free-form question: how many chained facts it needs, whether a hop needs live web information, a category, a confidence level, and one short explaining sentence — offered as a dismissible suggestion, bypassed for presets.
surfaces.affordance: present as a suggestion the user can accept or dismiss

invocation.trigger: Visitor submits or blurs the free-form question field in the ReAct Loop example (debounced), or presses Start with a custom question and no cached verdict exists. Skipped entirely when one of the five curated presets is selected — presets carry a hardcoded verdict.

surfaces.name: react_trace_stream
surfaces.output: A progressively filled trace of cycles — each with the model's short thought, the action it chose (exact query issued, or its decision to answer), and the verbatim observation returned — with a live cycle counter, ending in exactly one of a final-answer card naming the observations it used or a budget-exhausted card naming what remained unresolved.
surfaces.affordance: stream the output progressively (streaming/typing indicator); show multi-step progress/status while it runs

invocation.trigger: Visitor opens the ReAct Loop example, selects one of five curated multi-hop presets or types their own question, sets a cycle budget, and presses Start; frontend calls POST /api/react/run

surfaces.name: react_hop_annotations
surfaces.output: A post-run badge and panel labelling each hop as observed (naming the supplying cycle) or recalled from the model's own knowledge, each with a one-line reason; never presents a budget-exhausted run as answered.
surfaces.affordance: runs in the background — surfaced as a status badge then a panel rather than a blocking wait

invocation.trigger: Fired once by the ReAct run controller when a run reaches a terminal state (final answer card or budget-exhausted card). Issued as a separate call after the loop closes, never inside a cycle; it does not consume the run's cycle budget.

surfaces.name: orch_overview
surfaces.output: Educational overview of fan-out / fan-in, the 3-call and 3-run quota rationale, and the contrast with peer multi-agent collaboration.

surfaces.name: orch_roster
surfaces.output: The fixed roster of four knowledge-only specialists, with the chosen pair flagged after the coordinator decides.

surfaces.name: orch_question_form
surfaces.output: Submitted question routed to the coordinator, with remaining runs shown.
surfaces.affordance: show multi-step progress/status while it runs

invocation.trigger: Two-phase, visitor-driven. Phase 1: visitor submits a question (curated preset or free-form) from the example app page → coordinator produces the delegation decision. Phase 2: visitor clicks the explicit 'Dispatch specialists' confirmation → the two chosen specialists run in parallel and the coordinator emits the merged answer.

surfaces.name: orch_delegation_decision
surfaces.output: Moderation verdict, the chosen pair with rationale, and a distinct brief per specialist — shown before anything is dispatched.
surfaces.affordance: require explicit confirmation before the action commits

invocation.trigger: Two-phase, visitor-driven. Phase 1: visitor submits a question (curated preset or free-form) from the example app page → coordinator produces the delegation decision. Phase 2: visitor clicks the explicit 'Dispatch specialists' confirmation → the two chosen specialists run in parallel and the coordinator emits the merged answer.

surfaces.name: orch_parallel_execution
surfaces.output: Two side-by-side specialist tracks with live per-track status, the brief each received, and its answer typed in progressively.
surfaces.affordance: stream the output progressively (streaming/typing indicator)

invocation.trigger: Two-phase, visitor-driven. Phase 1: visitor submits a question (curated preset or free-form) from the example app page → coordinator produces the delegation decision. surfaces.name: orch_merged_answer
surfaces.output: One merged answer reconciling both contributions, plus a comparison note listing agreements, complements and contradictions; when a specialist failed, the missing perspective is named rather than filled in.
surfaces.affordance: show fan-in progress while it runs

invocation.trigger: Two-phase, visitor-driven. Phase 1: visitor submits a question (curated preset or free-form) from the example app page → coordinator produces the delegation decision. Phase 2: visitor clicks the explicit 'Dispatch specialists' confirmation → the two chosen specialists run in parallel and the coordinator emits the merged answer.

surfaces.name: collab_overview
surfaces.output: Educational overview of peer collaboration, the code-enforced opacity claim, the A2A data-shape-without-transport note, and the candid staged-boundary / over-engineering framing plus the 6-call, 2-run budget.

surfaces.name: collab_agent_cards
surfaces.output: Inspectable identity cards for the buyer and both sellers (provider, skills, capabilities, tool access), with private constraints explicitly absent.

surfaces.name: collab_scenario_form

surfaces.name: collab_negotiation_tracks
surfaces.output: A stage rail plus the composed RFQ, two concurrent seller tracks with bid tables and typed notes for opening and best-and-final bids, and the buyer's two targeted counter-offers.
surfaces.affordance: stream the output progressively (streaming/typing indicator); show multi-step progress/status while it runs

invocation.trigger: Visitor selects a preset scenario and a priority weighting on the Multi-Agent Collaboration example page and clicks 'Start negotiation'; a single POST /api/examples/multi-agent/runs call starts the run.
